doc.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Sticking with music; closing words on age, health and the new normal
summary: At 76 with one lung, Butch says he is thrilled to be here, and advises sticking it out.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Well this has been a marvelous re-visiting with you and I want to wrap up — I’m going to read something that you said about basically careers in music and you said, “you have to stick in this business because it will kill you, it will just waste you away and then turn around and make your life so marvelous you can’t believe you ever thought of a rainy day as anything else except sunshine and beautiful blue skies. Then maybe the next day you’re back with clouds and thunderstorms.” I’m glad you stuck with it.

Well I’ll tell you, what am I now, yeah I’m 76 years old. I’ll be 77 next July. I got one decent lung. My body is falling apart. My feet are all busted up and my hands hurt. I take a myriad of medicine. That’s hard to say, wow. I wonder if I can copyright that phrase, “a myriad of medicine” every single day. I go to see the doctor a lot. And yet I’m just thrilled to be here. I hear something that excites me, I see something that gives me pleasure, I’m looking over your shoulder and I can finally make it out, you’ve got “Every Day” up there, you’ve got a score to “Every Day I Have the Blues.” Right?

I like that. That’s very, very nice. Because “Every Day I Have the Blues” good, bad or indifferent. And I’m just very happy to be here because sometimes I get a chance to have an opportunity to enjoy a little chat with an old friend that I haven’t seen for a long time like Monk Rowe.
So I’m very happy to be here. Just stick it out. Stick it out.

All right. Well I can’t think of a better way to wrap up, Butch, and keep doing it. I’m going to keep doing it. And things may not get back to normal but we’ll have something better than right now I’m sure.
It’ll be different, that’s for sure.
Yes indeed. Okay. Well thanks a lot.
